clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch with a warning at work, then separated from Celeste; your mother's anxiety rose over her mother and Anton; and your brother Callum had ear infections through that winter. The shifts pile up from February through May 1979, moving through the family in waves. Event 120, a conflict between Delphine and Simone over selling the house, cannot be dated and is left out.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1984–1997
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, within the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose overfunctioned with her care and argued with your father over how he kept the house; your father phoned his father every night with rising anxiety, then argued with his uncle Lyle over who should help their parents. Your father's drinking rose, and he fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house. Your aunt Pearl's anxiety rose as she drove. As Hazel's functioning fell through the 1990s, your grandfather gave up his workshop and stayed at her side; a nurse came each morning; and her move to the Fairlie home in June 1997 marks where the period settles. Earlier, in spring 1984 when your mother was ordered to bed in pregnancy, Hazel came to keep house and conflict with your father rose, and your brother stammered again. Event 133, your own anxiety about your father at bedtime in July, cannot be dated and is left out.

clusters.name: Callum's move north, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving home for work up north in May 1999, within the following year: he argued with your father most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage with falling functioning; your sister Ines skipped school through the autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere, turning toward her; and Ines returned to school full days and passed her exams by August 2000. Event 160, Callum beginning to phone your mother on Sunday nights, cannot be dated and is left out.

clusters.name: Gran Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within the following months: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night, stopped going in to the bookshop by April and lost the job in May, dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark by August, and took a job at the garden centre in November where you slept through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then. Event 167, your stopping to return your mother's calls, cannot be dated and is left out.
